claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar FCC/B2 dual-phase microstructure with an interlamellar spacing of about 2 μm.
The as-cast alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low room-temperature ductility.
Room-temperature or 200–300°C severe plastic deformation introduces a high dislocation density in this alloy.
Severe plastic deformation with true strain greater than 4 will break the continuity of the FCC/B2 lamellae.
Annealing at 600–700°C for 1–4 hours will cause interface migration and phase redistribution without full coarsening.
The combined SPD and annealing treatment will transform the continuous lamellae into discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous FCC matrix or into a reduced-aspect-ratio globularized network.
Dislocation pile-ups generated at phase interfaces during SPD mediate subsequent interface migration and phase separation during annealing.
Continuous lamellar interfaces act as preferential crack paths in the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy.
Breaking and redistributing the lamellae will relieve interfacial stress concentrations.
A continuous FCC matrix will promote uniform plasticity and dislocation glide.
Discrete B2 precipitates can retain strengthening while avoiding the poor ductility associated with a continuous ordered B2 phase.

In refractory BCC+B2 high-entropy alloys, an inverted microstructure consisting of discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix improves room-temperature compressive ductility while maintaining high yield strength.
The inverted-microstructure result from refractory BCC+B2 alloys can be adapted to an FCC/B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy under room-temperature uniaxial tension.
The proposed treatment will increase room-temperature tensile fracture strain to greater than 10%.
The proposed treatment will reduce catastrophic interfacial cracking while maintaining high yield strength.
Successful treatment requires remaining below the temperature at which B2 dissolves or the eutectic structure fully coarsens.
The applied strain must be high enough to break the lamellae but below the level causing amorphization or excessive grain refinement and premature failure.
The FCC phase in the specific AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has high stacking-fault energy that may alter its response to SPD.
Conventional HIP at 1200°C and 207 MPa is expected to be insufficient to produce the proposed patterned microstructure.
Failure of HIP to transform the microstructure would establish SPD as the critical factor responsible for any HITM effect.
